sections.h2: Where to take a deed in Roscommon County
sections.html:
Take it to the Roscommon County Register of Deeds, 500 Lake Street in the village of Roscommon, ZIP 48653. The office number is 989-275-5931 and the fax is 989-275-8640. Call ahead for counter hours, especially if you are driving in from Houghton Lake, Prudenville or St. Helen.

The county's Online Services page links a public record search, a separate sign-in for title companies and law offices, BS&A parcel and tax data, and a GIS parcel map. Pull the prior deed and the legal description there before anything is drafted.

Parcels here are spread out, with lakefront lots around Houghton Lake and Higgins Lake and woodland near the Au Sable State Forest. Interstate 75 clips the northeast, US 127 follows the western edge of both lakes, and M-18 and M-55 cross near the middle, so a trip to the counter is easy from most of the county.

Filing is a flat $30 for each document, whether it is a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens. If one document releases or assigns several earlier instruments, add $3 for each additional one. The register's fee page lists these extras:

  • Photocopies at $1 a page, plus $5 when certified.
  • Faxed copies at $2 plus $1 a page.
  • Mailed copies at $5.
  • Emailed copies at $2 plus $1 a page.

E-recording is limited. The county takes no certified documents electronically except death certificates, so a signed deed arrives at the counter or by post. Ask the office how the check should be made out and whether to enclose a prepaid return envelope.

sections.h2: Documents that need a treasurer's certificate first
sections.html:
The register will not file a warranty deed, a deed with any warranty covenant, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract, a condominium master deed or a covenant deed until the County Treasurer has issued a tax certificate. The treasurer's fee is a separate $5 payment for up to 25 parcel descriptions, with 20 cents for every description after that, made out to the County Treasurer.

The rule comes from MCL 211.135. A certificate has to show no tax liens or tax titles on the parcel and that the preceding five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim deed with no warranty falls outside the section, and that is why many family transfers skip it.

sections.h2: Who owes transfer tax on a sale?
sections.html:
The seller carries this tax, and the treasurer's office takes the payment. Under the state act the money falls due a little over two weeks after the deed changes hands, and it attaches to deeds and sale contracts made for consideration (MCL 207.523). A county levy of $0.55 for each $500 band of value also applies where the population is below two million (MCL 207.504). The deed has to show its full value on its face, or an affidavit giving that value is attached. A deed that mixes real and personal property can state the two values separately so only the land is taxed.

Plenty of conveyances owe nothing. The state act exempts transfers under $100, deeds to a son, daughter or grandchild, transfers by foreclosure or deed in lieu, court orders that name no price, and quitclaim deeds that fix a defect in title (MCL 207.526). A seller who paid and later decides the sale qualified can ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

sections.h2: How a recorded sale changes the tax bill
sections.html:
Two notices reach the assessor. The office passes recorded transfers to local assessing officers at least monthly, and the buyer sends the assessor a transfer form no later than 45 days after closing. After a transfer, the taxable value is reset to state equalized value for the following year (MCL 211.27a). A cabin held since the 1970s can therefore carry a much higher bill under its next owner.

The county has 23,069 housing units for 23,459 residents, and 50.5% of those units are vacant, the mark of a seasonal market. Owners occupy 81.5% of the homes that have year-round residents.

Assessing is done by the townships and the village, so valuation questions belong with the local assessor named on the bill. The county treasurer issues certificates and takes transfer tax, and the Register of Deeds files the instrument itself.

sections.h2: Land contracts and long chains of title
sections.html:
The county grew fast after the war, from 2,055 residents in 1930 to 16,374 in 1980 and a peak of 25,469 in 2000. Parcels with long chains of deeds are common, so a title search can run back many owners.

Where a property was bought on a land contract, remember that the contract and the later deed are separate instruments. A land contract needs the treasurer's certificate, and under MCL 211.27a its taxable value resets for the year after the contract is signed, with no second reset once the deed is on file.

Start with the parcel record on the county's search page, and confirm the owner of record, the legal description and any open mortgage. Then run through this list:

  • Decide whether the deed will carry a warranty covenant, because that triggers the certificate.
  • Request the certificate and the transfer tax amount from the treasurer ahead of closing.
  • State the full value on the deed, or prepare the valuation affidavit.
  • Phone 989-275-5931 for counter hours and how to submit the original.

Plan the order of events so nothing waits on another office. The treasurer's certificate has to exist before the register can file a warranty deed, and the transfer tax is due soon after the deed is delivered. If the buyer is paying with a loan, the lender will want the recorded deed back quickly, so ask the title agent how it plans to deliver the original and which office it expects to visit first.

Keep every receipt. The treasurer's payment, the recording fee and the transfer tax each come from a different step, and your closing statement should show all three so you can match them later.

A buyer's title agent will flag any lien, prior mortgage or unreleased discharge that shows in the record search, so clear those first. A cash buyer needs the same certificate, deed and tax payment. What a cash sale skips is lender underwriting, so closing can move faster once the treasurer's paperwork is in hand.

faqs.q: What is the fee to file a deed in Roscommon County?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, with $3 more for each extra instrument that one document assigns or discharges. Copies cost $1 a page and certification adds $5.

faqs.q: Is a treasurer's certificate needed for a quitclaim deed here?
faqs.a: Usually not, since a quitclaim deed with no warranty is outside MCL 211.135. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts need the certificate from the County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can a Roscommon County deed be e-recorded?
faqs.a: Mostly no. The county accepts no certified documents electronically apart from death certificates, so deeds go to the counter or through the mail.

faqs.q: Whose job is the transfer tax on a Roscommon County sale?
faqs.a: The seller covers it, and the county treasurer takes the payment inside the same short window. Conveyances to a son, daughter or grandchild, foreclosures and transfers under $100 are exempt.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches the Roscommon County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 989-275-5931, or fax 989-275-8640. The office is at 500 Lake Street in Roscommon.
